Items.Authors: Jun W. W. Li, Kai Zhang, Zhaoying Zheng, Shun Li
Items.Title: Optomechanical structural design and dynamic performance analysis of a large-inertia fast steering mirror for astronomical image stabilization
Items.Abstract: To address image jitter in astronomical spectrometers, this paper presents the design of a large-inertia Fast Steering Mirror (FSM) carrying a 175 mm mirror (~2 kg payload). A cross-layout dual right-circular flexure hinge mechanism is proposed to ensure structural stiffness. The system is driven by four voice coil motors (VCMs) delivering a maximum continuous force of 110 N, utilizing four differential eddy current sensors for feedback. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) indicates resonant frequencies of ~100 Hz in working directions and >200 Hz in non-working directions. Experimental results confirm a maximum stroke of 1000 arcseconds and a closed-loop bandwidth of 30–40 Hz. The proposed design successfully balances high load capacity with dynamic response requirements.

Items.Authors: Luis V. Rodriguez de Marcos, Virginia D. Wheeler, Maria G. Sales, Javier G. Del Hoyo, Mateo F. Batkis, Manuel A. Quijada, Edward J. Wollack, Scott G. Walton, David R. Boris
Items.Title: Overview of plasma-based processes for the passivation of broadband aluminum mirror coatings for UV space telescopes
Items.Abstract: Efficient and uniform Aluminum-based broadband mirrors are essential components for FUV/UV/O/IR (λ=100-2500 nm) astronomy. An ongoing collaboration between the U.S. NRL and NASA GSFC focuses on optimization of AlF3 layers grown on Al mirrors to enhance FUV/UV/O/IR performance.   In previous work we demonstrated a new process based on e-beam generated plasmas for fluorinating the surface of Al mirrors.   More recently, we have demonstrated high quality AlF3 films growth on Al mirrors through the highly conformal plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) process. This approach can lead to new coating designs.  Both processes have demonstrated high FUV/UV/O/IR reflectivity, high quality AlF3 layers, low surface roughness, good coating uniformity of the fluoride layer, low coating-induced polarization aberration, and improved durability.   This presentation shows an overview of both processes and related TRL advancement works.

Items.Authors: Benjamin Calvin, Rose Gibson, Michael Fitzgerald, Jason Fucik, Evan Kress, Eric Wang, Chris Johnson, Jake Zimmer, James Wiley, Tim Greffe, Don Neill, Rishi Pahuja, Takayuki Kotani, Ashley Baker, Sam Halverson, Nemanja Jovanovic, Dimitri Mawet
Items.Title: Overview of the alignment plan for the Keck/HISPEC spectrometer subsystem
Items.Abstract: The High-Resolution Infrared Spectrometer for Exoplanet Characterization (HISPEC) will use fiber-fed optics to deliver R~100,000 spectroscopy across the y, J, H, and K bands for the Keck Observatory. The science light is separated with the yJ light measured in the BSPEC spectrometer, and the HK light in the RSPEC spectrometer. The contents of these spectrometers include an initial tri-mirror anistigmat (TMA) relay to collimate science light from the fiber subsystem, reflective Germanium gratings to disperse and cross-disperse the light, and then a second TMA to bring the spectrally dispersed light to a focus at an H4RG-10 detector. In these proceedings, we present the procedure for the optical alignment of the spectrometers. We use a coordinate measuring machine to place the TMA mirrors into 3D space in accordance with our optical design and then use a Zygo interferometer to verify the double-pass optical wavefront error of each TMA relay at both warm and cryogenic temperatures.

Items.Authors: Ana Guijarro, Matthias Alter, Peter Bizenberger, María Concepción Cárdenas Vázquez, Bernhard Dorner, Matilde Fernández, Julia Gallego, Antonio J. García Segura, Jens Helmling, Armin Huber, José Miguel Ibáñez, Ulrich Mall, Richard J. Mathar, Sara Muñoz Torres, Vianak Naranjo
Items.Title: PANIC4K - from the lab to the sky: What you don't know and would like to know about this camera
Items.Abstract: PANIC4K is a wide-field near-infrared camera with a monolithic HAWAII-4RG detector for the 2.2m telescope at the Calar Alto Observatory in Spain.  In this work, the PANIC4K team (MPIA, IAA-CSIC, and CAHA) presents solutions to problems encountered with the detector performance, details the process of the non-linearity correction, and shows the capabilities and improvements of its software packages: GEIRS for the data acquisition and mechanisms control, the Observation Tool (OT) for executing observations, and the quick-look (PQL) and pipeline (PAPI) for the preliminary data processing. In addition, the team presents preliminary results from the first scientific observations carried out after commissioning, conducted by groups from several Spanish and international institutions.

Items.Authors: Jérôme Maire, Alyssa Johnson, Wei Liu, Shelley A. Wright, Aaron Brown, Benjamin Godfrey, Jamie Holder, Nikolas Korzoun, Andrew Howard, Paul Horowitz, Yuriy Popovych, Elisa Pueschel, Nicolas Rault-Wang, Sruthiranjani Ravikularaman, Dan Werthimer
Items.Title: Panoramic SETI: experimental deployment at Palomar Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Panoramic Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (PANOSETI) project is designed to detect fast optical transients spanning nanosecond-to-second timescales, including ultra-high-energy phenomena, time-domain astrophysical events, and potential technosignatures.  The deployment of multiple wide-field optical telescopes equipped with fast, synchronized detectors and separated by hundred-meter baselines enables precise parallax measurements that discriminate atmospheric Cherenkov air showers from distant astrophysical sources. Increasing the number of telescopes further improves the achievable angular resolution needed to localize the origin of gamma-ray–induced shower events.   Here we report on the first deployment and integration of a four-telescope array at Palomar Observatory. We present the technical implementation, operational strategy, and initial on-sky performance of this multi-telescope transient observatory.

Items.Authors: Alyssa Johnson, Jerome Maire, Shelley Wright, Aaron Brown, Benjamin Godfrey, Jamie Holder, Paul Horowitz, Andrew Howard, Nikolas Korzoun, Wei Liu, Yuriy Popovych, Elisa Pueschel, Nico Rault-Wang, Sruthiranjani Ravikularaman, Dan Werthimer
Items.Title: Panoramic SETI: on-sky results at Palomar Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Panoramic SETI (PANOSETI) project is deploying wide-field optical telescopes at Palomar Observatory to search for nanosecond-scale fast transients. We present the first on-sky performance results from newly commissioned modules, including background measurements in multiple observing modes, point-source detection limits, and timing stability. We report the false-alarm rate in Pulse Height mode and demonstrate coincidence-based rejection across multiple telescopes. Early science observations targeting astrophysical point sources are described, along with initial steps toward a SETI survey. These results establish PANOSETI’s readiness for routine transient searches and technosignature observations.

Items.Authors: Frédéric J. Grandmont
Items.Title: Paradigm shift cooking in sub-meter space telescope…
Items.Abstract: While internet mega-constellations undesired impact dominate astronomy discourse, a quieter revo-lution in Earth Observation (EO) is in full motion. Feeding from the new satellite commodity echo-system, bold entrepreneurs are committed to bring space-based optical observation to the masses. Heightened international tensions also encouraging intelligence imagery independence, startups and legacy suppliers are now engaged in large-aperture high-resolution or wide-field multi-detectors tele-scope-camera systems. Using relevant project examples, we explore how modern private EO satellites could perform if pointed toward deep-space and review the compromises needed to get to the price point enabling investor’s business cases. This surge of new funding in technologies highly relevant to astronomy instrumentation is changing the space access equation. We aim to demonstrate how these advances directly benefit candidate astronomy missions such as POET, TWINKLE, and CASTOR.

Items.Authors: Pilar Montañés-Rodríguez
Items.Title: Parameter analysis for optical polishing in the OptoTech MCP1501 with cross-machine consistency to IRP600
Items.Abstract: The Centro de Sistemas Ópticos Avanzados (CSOA) at the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias has recently expanded with the addition of CSOA15 —a laboratory focused on large-aperture optical polishing that complements the existing CSOA05 facility for small and mid-size components. At CSOA15, the OptoTech MCP1501 is the main platform for polishing optics up to 1500 mm.   Optical polishing on machines such as the MCP1501 depends on a complex interplay of process parameters, including pad state, trajectory pattern, slurry transport, friction regime and thermal behaviour, all of which are difficult to quantify and often exhibit coupled uncertainties. We present a parameter-focused analysis aimed at identifying the variables that most strongly influence surface evolution in the MCP1501 and establish a cross-machine comparison with the IRP600 to evaluate parameter consistency and machine-specific behaviour. A Bayesian inference framework is implemented to capture uncertainty, parameter c

Items.Authors: Kazuo Yoshioka, Yudai Suzuki, Ashita Yamazaki, Yusei Mitoh, Makoto Taguchi, Masaki Kuwabara, Madoka Endo
Items.Title: Performance evaluation of optical components dedicated to Lyman-α observations from ultra-small spacecraft
Items.Abstract: This study presents the design principles and performance evaluation of optical components optimized for hydrogen Lyman-α (121.6 nm) observations in compact ultraviolet imaging systems, including those onboard ultra-small spacecraft. UV mirrors, spectral filters, and the detector assembly were developed to achieve high reflectance, narrow-band selectivity (for separating H and D Lyman-α), and stable detection efficiency under strict constraints on size, mass, and power. Our laboratory measurements of reflectance, filter transmission, and detector response demonstrate that these components exhibit performance comparable to that of instruments used in larger-scale missions. As an application, these results are being applied to the development of the Hydrogen Imager (HI), a compact UV instrument planned for a JAXA probe participating in ESA’s Comet Interceptor mission.

Items.Authors: Taewan Kim, Yuki Moritani, Chi-Hung Yan, Shiang-Yu Wang, Jennifer Karr, Craig P. Loomis, Shitaro Koshida, Naoyuki Tamura
Items.Title: Performance evaluation of PFS fiber positioner, Cobra, using accumulated operational data
Items.Abstract: The Prime Focus Spectrograph (PFS) / ʻŌnohiʻula on the Subaru Telescope is a multi-object spectrograph employing nearly 2,400 robotic fiber positioners, named Cobras, to place fibers onto astronomical targets. We present a comprehensive evaluation of Cobra positioning performance and the pipelines developed for routine monitoring. The analysis focuses on three metrics: geometry, which characterizes the center positions, arm lengths, and rotational ranges of Cobras; motor maps, which describe angular-dependent motor movement speeds; and convergence, which quantifies how closely Cobras reach their assigned targets. Using the accumulated PFS operational dataset from 2023 to 2025, we assess the long-term behavior of these metrics as functions of telescope position and operational epoch. The resulting performance trends provide essential guidance for optimizing Cobra motions during observations. We developed a publicly accessible dashboard that presents all evaluated metrics for PFS users.

Items.Authors: Ebru UZUNÇAM, Burak Bülent Güçsav, Onur Şatır, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: Performance metrics for DAG400 Telescope
Items.Abstract: The performance of 4-m class telescopes like the DAG400 Telescope depends on the coordination of optical, mechanical, thermal, and control subsystems rather than image quality alone. This work presents an integrated framework that correlates these domains using long-term observational and engineering data. Key metrics include pointing and tracking logs, image quality, PSF stability, wavefront error, tracking-error statistics, and dome- and mirror-seeing contributions, along with thermal effects. The analysis summarizes the performance criteria of such areas as optimization, such as improved control algorithms, enhanced thermal management, and possible subsystem upgrades.

Items.Authors: Stephen A. Smee, Aidan C. Gray, Stephen C. Hope, Randolph P. Hammond, Albert J. Harding, Tyson S. Hare, Leon Aslan, Andrea Bianco, Christoph Birk, Maren Cosens, Michele Frangiamore, Daniel D. Kelson, Gerrad Killian, Nicholas P. Konidaris, Alicia E. Lanz, Jacob McCloskey, Andrew B. Newman, Solange Ramírez, Gwen C. Rudie, Andrea Vanella, Jason E. Williams
Items.Title: Performance of the MIRMOS cryogenic mechanism for detector dithering and flexure compensation
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of an X-Y stage for detector dithering and flexure compensation. The mechanism is being developed for the Magellan InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph, MIRMOS. This cryogenically cooled instrument utilizes five science cameras, each having a custom X-Y stage to control in-plane detector position, providing dithering capability for improved sampling, and flexure compensation to correct for gravity-induced image motion. With a design operating temperature of 120 K, the piezo-driven flexure stage provides high-resolution backlash-free motion of the detector in a compact form-factor that minimizes camera length. A calibrated magnetoresistive sensor on each axis provides PID-controlled feedback for accurate, repeatable positioning. Here, we present the design of a second-generation prototype, as well as performance results from recent cryogenic testing.

Items.Authors: Oliver Pineda Suárez, Malak Galal, Jonathan Wei, Maxime Rombach, Sébastien Pernecker, Jean-Paul Kneib
Items.Title: Performance testing of a trillium-based 21-positioner module for stage-5 telescopes
Items.Abstract: Evaluating the performance metrics of micro-SCARA robotic positioners is crucial to gather insights into the system’s behavior and ensure their reliability during operation in Stage-5 telescopes. In this paper we present the results of the positioning performance and angular tilt tests conducted on 6.2-mm-pitch robotic positioner modules developed for high-density fiber positioning in next-generation astronomical systems. The fiber positioners from the tested prototype adopt a mechanical design based on the Trillium open design from the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL) and were produced by the Japanese company Orbray. The positioners exhibited a generally acceptable performance, although noticeable anomalies affecting several metrics were identified and will require mitigation in subsequent prototypes. Nevertheless, the results indicate promising performance suitable for Stage-5 telescope instrumentation, provided that these issues are successfully resolved.

Items.Authors: Marina Centenera-Merino, Jesús Aceituno, Pedro José Amado, Miguel Andrés Sánchez-Carrasco, Javier Flores, Julius Goehring, Sergio Leon-Saval, Kalaga Madhav, Abani Nayak, José Luis Ortiz, David Peréz-Medialdea, Francisco José Pozuelos, Martin M. Roth, María Isabel Ruíz, Stefan Cikota
Items.Title: Photonic EMARCOT at Calar Alto: astrophotonic lab at the IAA-CSIC
Items.Abstract: The Photonic E-MARCOT project introduces a scalable, modular, and cost-effective astronomical architecture. Its first phase, the MARCOT Pathfinder, is currently operating at the Calar Alto Observatory with an array of seven small telescopes designed to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio.  The system relies on advanced photonic technology developed at the IAA-CSIC Astrophotonic Lab, focusing on device fabrication, full optical characterisation, and studies of the quantum nature of light. Although high-precision equipment is now available to manufacture efficient photonic components, their optical behaviour still requires more detailed characterisation. A comprehensive protocol is therefore being developed to assess efficiency, stability, and performance. This will optimize current devices and guide the creation of future photonic architectures and quantum-technology applications.

Items.Authors: Avi Patel, Kevin Bundy, Aditya Sengupta, Matthew DeMartino, Anna Gagnebin, Emiel Por, Majid Mohammad, Michael Arena, Aled Cuda, Kiana Ejercito, Stephen Eikenberry, Ben Mazin, Holger Schmidt
Items.Title: Photonic lantern design on a chip
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns (PLs) convert multimode light into single-mode channels for high-precision spectroscopy and wavefront sensing, but conventional fiber PLs are fragile, difficult to manufacture, and challenging to scale. We present the design of a four-port on-chip PL using ANSYS Lumerical FDTD, developed in collaboration with the Mazin Lab at UC Santa Barbara. Our integrated approach enables fabrication using standard photonic-chip processes, offering improved robustness and repeatability. Simulations provide insight into mode-coupling efficiency and throughput, which are difficult to measure experimentally due to unobservable internal mode evolution. We also explore inverse-design strategies for a future 19-port broadband PL to support more advanced routing architectures. Our goal is to realize compact, stable single-mode spectroscopy on a chip, enabling scalable, low-cost photonic devices for next-generation astronomical instruments.

Items.Authors: David Kappel, Martin Pertenais, Nicolas Gorius, Matthias Ammler-von Eiff, Sascha Grziwa, Demetrio Magrin, Matteo Munari, Pierre Royer, Juan Cabrera, Denis Griessbach, Thierry Appourchaux, Gonzalo Ramos, M. Teresa Rodrigo, Angel L. Valverde, Elisa Borreguero, Francisco Montoro, M. Ángeles Sierra, Lucia Espinosa, Fernando Conde, Amaia Santiago, Jesus Saiz, Lorenza Ferrari, Ann Baeke, Heike Rauer
Items.Title: PLATO camera ghosts: characterization of geometry and intensity from TVAC measurements of the flight models and the engineering model
Items.Abstract: The upcoming PLATO mission (Rauer et al., 2025) will, among others, discover and characterize thousands of exoplanets and is designed to reach the regime of Earth-like planets in the habitable zone of solar-type stars. Here we evaluate results of TVAC measurement campaigns performed in three different test houses in comparison to simulations for the characterization of optical ghosts in seven camera flight models and the engineering model. We investigated intensities and geometries of extended and point-like ghosts, emerging from parasitic reflections of incoming light in the optical system, as these can impact the scientific observations of PLATO. We found the ghost intensities to be well within the requirement specifications. The locations and sizes of the ghosts very well agree between the different cameras and with the simulations. Our findings prepare a camera-specific prediction of the ghost intensities and geometries for PLATO in flight.

Items.Authors: Giuseppe Crescenzio, Gabriele Carozzi, Leonardo Cavicchiolo, Alexandre Cabral, Nuno Santos
Items.Title: PoET solar observatory opto-mechanical solutions
Items.Abstract: The presented solar telescope is a Gregorian system with a 600 mm aperture and f/12 focal ratio, optimized for high-resolution solar observations. An intermediate focus hosts a heat rejector (Heat Stop) to manage thermal load, protecting instruments and ensuring stability. The optical design, with precisely aligned mirrors, minimizes aberrations and guarantees focal plane accuracy. The opto-mechanical interface supports advanced instruments like spectropolarimeters and high-speed imagers for studies of solar dynamics, magnetic fields, and transient phenomena. Mounted on an Altazimuth fork, the system offers high stiffness and stability. Direct-drive motors with high-resolution encoders and on-sky calibration deliver accurate pointing and tracking without backlash. This paper details the design, manufacturing, and technological solutions adopted to meet demanding scientific and engineering requirements.

Items.Authors: Shuangquan Chen, Qihang Zhang, Shuo Wang, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Portable platform based on smart phones: wireless testing and OTA firmware upgrade for LAMOST optical fiber positioning units
Items.Abstract: To address the challenges posed by the significant increase in the number of LAMOST fiber optic positioning units for testing and maintenance, this paper has developed a portable wireless control and firmware update platform based on smart phones. This system includes a self-developed Android application, a micro wireless control board based on STM32 and a Bluetooth communication link, completely getting rid of the reliance on traditional upper computers and wired burners. Through the mobile phone APP, users can conduct wireless driver tests on individual or multiple units (supporting single/continuous runing-in), and can directly complete the wireless upgrade of child node firmware and ID reconfiguration at the installation site by using Bluetooth OTA technology. This platform significantly enhances the flexibility, portability and efficiency of operation, providing an innovative solution for on-site commissioning and maintenance of large-scale astronomical instruments.

Items.Authors: Joonas Viuho, Anton N. Sørensen, Amanda A. Djupvik, Michael I. Andersen, Johan P. Fynbo, Lise B. Christensen
Items.Title: Practical experience using KDP as a thermal blocking filter
Items.Abstract: Monopotassium dihydrogen phosphate (KDP, chemical formula KH2PO4) is a material with many use cases ranging from agricultural fertilizer to a frequency modulator in near infrared lasers. One of its optical properties is high transparency from ultraviolet to 1.3µm, while being practically fully opaque at wavelengths longer than 1.8µm making it an ideal shortpass filter the near infrared. However, a few practical drawbacks exist and we will share our experiences using KDP filters at observatory conditions.

Items.Authors: Thansita Thomrungpiyathan, Samattachai Tanun, Krittapas Chanchaiworawit, Teerawat Kuha, Auychai Laoyang, Tarathon Intaros, Picha Ruenarrom, Manlika Pinkaew, Apichat Leckngam, Wiphu Rujopakarn
Items.Title: Precision enhancement and production-cost reduction in a multi-stage optical manufacturing workflow via CNC parameter optimization for astronomical and space systems
Items.Abstract: NARIT has developed an integrated optical-manufacturing workflow that combines CNC machining, single-point diamond turning (SPDT), and high-accuracy CMM metrology for producing mirrors, mounts, and precision opto-mechanical components for astronomical and spaceborne applications. CNC machining serves as the primary pre-processing stage, strengthened through improved CAM orientation, zero-deformation fixturing, and refined control of feed rate, cutting depth, tool engagement, and thermal-compensation strategies. These enhancements greatly improve tolerance stability, reduce rework cycles, and increase overall production efficiency. CMM measurements confirm notable gains in form error, repeatability, and dimensional stability, with clear benefits for lightweight or thin-walled components. Collectively, these advancements enable a more reliable, scalable, and cost-effective CNC–SPDT–CMM workflow to support precision optical manufacturing.

Items.Authors: Léonard Lebrun, Johannes Wüthrich, Andrin Fazan, Sean MacBride, Felipe Andrade-Oliveira, Marcelle Soares-Santos
Items.Title: Precision measurements of the axial drift in fiber positioners for spectroscopic surveys using defocus blur
Items.Abstract: Aiming for new breakthroughs in cosmology, the next-generation spectroscopic surveys will use robotic fiber positioners in the focal plane of large aperture telescopes to simultaneously observe tens of thousands of targets. To achieve this ambitious goal, the mechanical stability of the positioners is critical. In this work, we present a test setup using defocus blur to assess the stability along the optical axis of a multi-fiber positioner module, aiming for a precision of 5 micrometers, in line with the requirements of several upcoming experiments. The test is performed both on an optical table and on a telescope mount that simulates the motions expected for an actual astronomical instrument. This defocus test setup may be used for characterization of prototypes during the R&D phase as well as for quality control during the production phase, ensuring that axial drifts in the positioners remain within the survey requirements.

Items.Authors: Pierce Morgan
Items.Title: Precision monolithic telescope assemblies for space: design advantages, demonstrated performance, and scaling production for flight systems
Items.Abstract: The Monolithic Telescope technology, developed at LLNL and now being commercialized by Starris Space Systems of Optimax, offers an innovative optical architecture for compact, highly stable space payloads. Made from a single piece of fused silica with primary and secondary surfaces polished on opposite sides, the Monolith removes alignment structures while maintaining diffraction-limited performance. Compared to Cassegrain designs, it provides reduced length and mass, excellent optical quality, and strong resilience to vibration, shock, and thermal variation, enabling high-performance imaging on smaller spacecraft with lower SWaP. Several configurations have been space-qualified or flown, demonstrating maturity and manufacturability. This talk reviews the transition from LLNL research to producible systems, including design and manufacturing methods, test results, and efforts to extend the technology to new mission classes and optical configurations.

Items.Authors: Pieter Vuylsteke, Bart Vandenbussche, Wim De Meester, Kwinten Missiaen, Jesus Perez Padilla, Gert Raskin, Wim Pessemier, Johan Morren, Saskia Prins, Jacob Pember, Kaustubh Hakim, Alexis Brandeker, Christian Schwab, Manuel Güdel, Benjamin Montet, Denis Defrère, Hans Van Winckel
Items.Title: Precision photometry with the MARVEL Telescope Array
Items.Abstract: MARVEL is a new facility intended for precision Doppler spectroscopy. The four robotic 0.8m telescopes have been installed in 2025. We have commissioned a precision photometry mode to commence early science observations, while the facilities Echelle spectrometer is being assembled. Here we report on operation of the facility, the implementation of the photometry capability, and results achieved so far.

Items.Authors: Joice Mathew
Items.Title: Probing interstellar dust from space: mapping the 2175 Å feature with the UVESS small satellite
Items.Abstract: Ultraviolet dust extinction complicates the characterization of stars and galaxies. The 2175 Å bump—the strongest UV extinction feature—varies across sightlines and hints at dust grain composition, yet its origin remains uncertain due to limited data. To address this, ANU and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics are developing UVESS (Ultraviolet Extinction Sky Survey), a small satellite carrying a compact UV spectrograph and MCP detector. Covering 1500–3000 Å at R≈200, UVESS will map thousands of sightlines, expanding current coverage tenfold. By integrating infrared datasets (e.g., Spitzer GLIMPSE, SPHEREx), the mission will explore links between the 2175 Å bump and PAH grains, advancing understanding of interstellar dust.

Items.Authors: Kun Chen, Wen Chen, Yingquan Yang, Xuliang Duan, Yang Gao, Genjian Qin, Xinyu Liu, Duojin Zheng, Siran Ding, Xu Wu, Dongxiao Xu, Qixing Wang, Yifei Wang, Na Meng, Zhiming Cai, Rong Shu, Jian Ge, Hui Zhang, Yongshuai Zhang, Weicheng Zang, Hongjing Yang, Shude Mao, Yutian Fu, Yonghe Chen, Feng Dong, Zongxi Song, Wei Gao, Hongfei Zhang, Jian Wang, Lianguo Wang, Yongmei Wang
Items.Title: Progress of the Earth 2.0 space spacecraft system design
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) mission is a next-generation Chinese space mission to detect thousands of Earth-sized planets, including habitable Earth-like planets orbiting solar type stars (Earth 2.0s), cold low-mass planets, and free floating planets. The ET mission will enter its Phase C study in 2026. During the Phase B study, detailed design and optimization of the spacecraft system were carried out, and several key aspects were updated to better fulfill the scientific requirements. In particular, the pointing stability requirement has been increased by more than one order of magnitude. This paper presents the progress in the ET spacecraft system design, covering the overall configuration, pointing stability control, scientific data download, and other aspects.

Items.Authors: Varun Shah, Vincenzo Cotroneo, Jose Antonio Dieste, Alejandro P. Marques, Maria Hernandez, Gil Moretto
Items.Title: Progress of Thermal-Forming of Normal-Incidence Glass Optics for the LiveMirror project
Items.Abstract: Thermal-forming of glass optics is the process of slumping thin glass sheets onto a mold using a suitable thermal cycle. This is a cost-effective process to fabricate high-performing light mirrors from readily available materials. The ‘EIC Live-Mirror’ project aims to produce lightweight, thermally-formed mirrors that are actively supported by electro-active polymer-based actuators. We perform slumping tests on stainless steel mandrels and analyze the figure and surface roughness of the produced samples to optimize the thermal-forming process, constrain the transfer of spatial frequencies, and ascertain what parameters introduce specific errors to guide the overall slumping process and the mandrel manufacturing requirements for larger optics.

Items.Authors: Thomas Schneider
Items.Title: Progress on a new M2 for the Gemini North telescope to minimize mechanical support print-through effects
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Observatory is procuring a new secondary mirror (M2) for the Gemini North telescope to improve image quality by minimizing print-through deformations. The M2 was replaced in 2008, but the root cause of the print-through was not properly addressed and was actually worsened. The current M2 at Gemini North suffers from approximately ± 1µm of surface deformation, resulting in an approximate 20% reduction in Strehl ratio. Finite element analysis(FEA) of the M2 and its support system has identified the root cause of the print-through. By making several changes to the mechanical supports, FEA has shown that the surface deformation can be reduced to approximately ±25nm or less. This paper details the root cause of the print-through effects and the design changes that will be made to the new M2 mechanical supports that will remediate them in the new M2. The current progress of the M2 fabrication is also detailed.

Items.Authors: Changhui Rao, Youming Guo, Lanqiang Zhang, Xuejun Rao
Items.Title: Progress on astronomical adaptive optics in NLAO, China
Items.Abstract: This presentation reports recent progress by China’s National Laboratory of Adaptive Optics (NLAO), established in 2024. In night-time astronomy, we are developing key AO systems: an AO/GLAO system with a 930mm deformable secondary mirror and four sodium laser guide stars (Na LGS) for a 4.2m telescope, and a Nasmyth AO system with cascade DMs for a 14.5m telescope. The Na LGS technology was successfully tested on-sky in 2025. For solar observation, the 1.8m Chinese Large Solar Telescope (CLST) with a 457-element AO system is completed and scheduled for installation in 2027. An AO/GLAO system for a 2.5m solar telescope has completed indoor testing. New systems for prominence observation and MCAO upgrade are also underway. We are further developing a 60cm compact solar adaptive telescope for high-contrast imaging.

Items.Authors: Thomas Schneider, Cristian Moreno, Tomislav Vucina, Clayton Ah Hee, Claudio Araya
Items.Title: Progress on creating a durable UV-enhanced silver coating for the Gemini Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Observatory has been searching for a UV-enhanced silver coating that can be applied to the primary, secondary, and tertiary mirror that will allow for faster observations out to 350nm. The coating must allow for at least 80% reflectivity at 350nm without compromising reflectivity and emissivity in near-infrared wavelengths. The coating must survive for at minimum of 5 years between coatings without significant degradation from environmental stressors or in-situ washes. The coating must be able to be stripped with acids that are no more toxic than the current chemical stripping agents. The UV-enhanced coating must be able to produced with the 3 magnetrons that are mounted in the Gemini chamber. This paper reports on the successes, partial successes, failures and potential new paths forwards for producing a durable UV-enhanced silver coating for astronomical observatories.

Items.Authors: Tanguy Thibert, Célestin Libert, Jean-Yves Plesseria
Items.Title: Progress on the comet interceptor mission scan mirror assembly: integration, assembly and test campaign of the qualification model
Items.Abstract: Comet Interceptor is a fast-class mission in ESA’s Cosmic Vision Program comprising three spacecrafts. With a short development process challenge, it will be the first mission to visit a Long Period Comet that is starting its journey in the inner Solar System.  The Rotating Mirror Assembly is mounted on the Comet Interceptor spacecraft A, rotating a mirror facing the Comet Camera instrument. The rotation allows continuous observations during the flyby. It is composed of the Scan Mirror Assembly (SMA), the CSL’s contribution, and the Scan Mirror Electronics (SME) from Thales Alenia Space Switzerland. The SMA is constituted of mirror assembly with a baffle, a mirror, a dust shield, and a rotation mechanism below.  In this paper, the design of the SMA is presented, and the main result of the integration, assembly and test campaign of the Qualification Model (QM) are discussed. A conclusion presents the lessons learned during this qualification phase of this first fast-class mission.

Items.Authors: Ross C. McCurdy, Drew M. Miles, Jake A. McCoy, Fabien Grise, Randall L. McEntaffer
Items.Title: Progress updates on blazed UV grating development with electron-beam lithography and TASTE
Items.Abstract: High performance UV reflection gratings are an essential technology for enabling key science objectives for HWO and potential future observatories in the coming decade. In recent years, funded NASA studies have developed electron-beam lithography (EBL) to write custom variable-line-space groove layouts. We will present on results of the development and optimization of EBL and the TASTE process to fabricate blazed UV gratings over a range of line densities and blaze angles. Specifically, we will discuss results from exploring the nanofabrication parameter space for UV grating fabrication with EBL and TASTE, limitations that we have encountered, and plans for fabricating larger format gratings at different periods and blaze angles for experimental testing and performance verification.

Items.Authors: Maider Insausti Múgica
Items.Title: Protected silver coatings at the IAC: monitoring the degradation of the reflectivity of the coatings at the Izaña Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Canary Islands Institute of Astrophysics (IAC) has been improving its capabilities for the design and manufacture of optical components for several years, especially the development of protective silver coatings for telescope mirrors up to 1.6 meters in diameter.    These mirrors are of great interest to the astronomical community due to their high reflectivity, but in harsh, sulfur-rich environments such as observatories, silver degrades very rapidly and Our current research focuses on improving the long-term stability and environmental resistance of silver coatings by optimizing deposition parameters and applying protective layers.

Items.Authors: Akira Rodziewicz-Ryan, Barnaby Norris, Christopher H. Betters, Julia J. Bryant, Laird M. Close, Daniel S. Dahl, Olivier Guyon, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Sergio Leon-Saval, Nathan K. Long, Jared R. Males, Andrew Ross-Adams
Items.Title: PWI-SPEC: an optical, multi-resolution spectrograph optimised for high fibre-count astrophotonic wavefront sensing and imaging instruments
Items.Abstract: Astrophotonic instruments have seen a recent surge of interest, including photonic integrated circuits and photonic lantern wavefront sensors and imagers. Their advancement, however, requires measurement of an ever-growing number of SM outputs, with specific spectral and temporal sampling demands, necessitating a spectrograph design dissimilar to current general purpose astronomical spectrographs. PWI-SPEC is an optical spectrograph being built at Astralis-USyd and SAIL for the Photonic Wavefront Imager (PWI) module of the MagAO-X extreme adaptive optics system, purpose-designed to accept 100s of SMFs by using a unique rotated 2D fibre matrix array, and offer both lower- and higher-resolution modes tailored to wavefront sensing and imaging respectively. The final spectra are imaged at optimal pixel sampling and separation onto an Andor CB2 sCMOS camera which allows 100 SMFs at low spectral resolution (R=90) to be read out at ~1000 frames per second, with 1.4 electrons read noise.

Items.Authors: Rui Zhang, Zhen Zhang, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Quantifying centroid shifts induced by glass in the GFA of JUST
Items.Abstract: The traditional star alignment methods mostly use spot projection to achieve the coordinate conversion between the focal plane fiber and the guide star camera (GFA). However, the guide star camera of the JUST Spectroscopic Telescope adopts a double-layer glass encapsulation structure. This special design introduces systematic errors caused by the glass-optical interface into the traditional star alignment method, and the deviation of the glass installation collimation will further affect the systematic error of the traditional calibration method. To quantify the above-mentioned errors, this thesis conducts an experiment on the extraction accuracy of the spot center for mask holes. By collecting spot images with or without glass, the spot center of gravity is extracted using the light center of gravity algorithm, and the absolute error of the Euclidean distance of spots with the same number is used as the measurement index for the offset of the spot center of gravity.

Items.Authors: Tara R. Crowe, Miguel Romer, Ameer Batarseh, Stephen Eikenberry, Rodrigo Amezcua-Correa, Daniel Cruz-Delgado, Stephanos Yerolatsitis, Miguel Bandres, Sergio Leon-Saval, Kerri Donaldson Hanna, Robert Conwell, Matthew Cooper, Caleb Dobias, Genevieve Markees, Christina Moraitis, David Smith, Aiden Akers, Vincent Miller, Sarah Thibaut
Items.Title: Quantum-Inspired Imaging (QI2) through atmospheric turbulence: on-sky results
Items.Abstract: Modal-basis imaging techniques facilitated by photonic lanterns (PLs) offer a unique method of focal-plane (FP) wavefront estimation. For large telescopes, atmospheric turbulence induces perturbations in the phase of a wavefront and is the most significant cause of image quality/resolution degradation. We demonstrate our PL-based wavefront sensor (WFS) to measure and correct wavefront fluctuations, both with and without the use of prior adaptive optics (AO) correction. By leveraging the wavelength sensitivity of PLs, our approach allows us to deduce turbulent phase variations over a broad wavelength range and break the degeneracy between atmospheric turbulence and diffraction, the latter of which is taken to be the fundamental resolution limit of traditional imaging systems. We present the design and on-sky results of two different quantum-inspired imaging systems and demonstrate our approach's efficacy for PL-WFS in the non-linear regime and with high-order wavefront aberrations.

Items.Authors: Remya B. S., Sriram Sripadmanabhan
Items.Title: Realuminization of 1 m Carl Zeiss Telescope Mirror and Reflectivity Degradation Studies at Vainu Bappu Observatory
Items.Abstract: The 1-m Carl Zeiss Ritchey–Chrétien telescope at the Vainu Bappu Observatory (VBO), Kavalur, underwent full re-aluminization using the calibrated 60-inch high-vacuum coating chamber. The old coating was chemically stripped and the mirror cleaned before aluminium deposition by thermal evaporation under ~10⁻⁶ mbar after ion-beam cleaning. The 36-filament firing unit ensured uniform vaporization. Witness samples showed a coating thickness of ~1210 Å (±100 Å) and ~90% reflectivity (365–970 nm) with <2% non-uniformity. Adhesion and pinhole tests confirmed coating integrity. The Cassegrain and Coudé mirrors achieved 88–89% reflectivity. Post-installation monitoring showed reflectivity declining from 90% to 75.4% over one year.

Items.Authors: Emily van Hese, Niek Doelman
Items.Title: Receiver diversity technology for satellite to ground low-loss free space optical communication
Items.Abstract: Free space optical communication promises high-data rate and high-security data links. Efficient ground station receiver design that mitigates atmospheric turbulence link losses is necessary to achieve this. Photonic technologies including few-mode fibres, adaptive optics to maintain optimal spot size and location in the receiver, and receiver diversity with multiple smaller apertures can each reduce atmospheric link losses. In this work, a numerical study is performed of these methods for a satellite-to-ground link in the presence of atmospheric phase and amplitude aberrations. Statistical analysis of instantaneous free-space to fibre coupling shows the changing distribution of coupled power under each mitigation method and under hybrid systems. The possibility and performance of combined solutions are presented.

Items.Authors: Francesco D'Alessio, Fabrizio Vitali, Emilio Molinari, Alberto Riva, Dino Fugazza, Giorgio Toso, Riccardo Belmonte, Bianca Salmaso, Andrés Gonzáles, Matteo Accardo, Veronika Wimmer, Gerd Jakob, Armin Silber, Ivo Saviane
Items.Title: REMIR cryogenics: from Yokohama to Copenhagen, two years of successful operations
Items.Abstract: REMIR is a NIR camera, mounted on the REM telescope at ESO-La Silla  Observatory. In 2024 we mounted the new Sunpower CryoTel GT AVC cryocooler, to replace the old CFC LN2 cooling system. The new cryocooler has showed a very good reliability and easeness of functioning. Since its installation (SPIE 2024), we improved the temperature control (to ensure a more stable detector temperature) and installed a redundant fan system (to avoid cryocooler stop, in case of a fan malfunctioning). In this paper, we report the performance data of this last 2 years and the description of the further improvement on the original system.

Items.Authors: Ria G. Krämer, Samuel L. Döpfner, Aashia Rahman, Georg R. Schwartz, Malte P. Siems, Daniel Richter, Kalaga Madhav, Stefan Nolte
Items.Title: Reproducible inscription of fiber Bragg gratings with ultrashort laser pulses for efficient multiple notch OH emission line filtering
Items.Abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) enable the suppression of hydroxyl (OH) sky emission, a major limitation in ground-based infrared astronomy. We present a robust fabrication method, using IR ultrashort laser pulses and a phase mask with integrated shaping apertures, providing tailored spectral profiles. Experimental validation on 20 distinct OH lines (1540-1590 nm) demonstrate exceptional reproducibility, with wavelength deviations below 60 pm and total throughputs exceeding 93%. These results confirm the potential of integrated aperture phase masks for realizing high-efficiency astronomical filters.

Items.Authors: Zhenshuai Yan, Yu Ye
Items.Title: Research on collaborative architecture optimization for computing offloading in telescope control of WeHoST
Items.Abstract: Aiming at the problems of response delay and resource occupation caused by the real-time coordinate calculation of the upper computer in the traditional architecture of the "WeHost" telescope, a collaborative optimization scheme of computing decentralization is proposed. The functions of calculating the coordinates of solar and night celestial bodies, GPS time correction and coordinate correction are migrated to the PMAC control system to achieve close coordination between operation and control instructions, reducing data transmission delay and the load on the upper computer. Experiments show that the optimized architecture significantly improves the real-time performance of coordinate calculation, the accuracy of time synchronization and the control response speed, providing stable support for the high-precision pointing control of the telescope.

Items.Authors: Baoyu Yang
Items.Title: Research on ultra-high stability thermal control design and verification for the space origin exploration program earth 2.0
Items.Abstract: The ultra-high stability thermal control design for the transit telescope payload of the Space Origin Exploration Program ET2.0. was conducted by leveraging the heat capacity of the controlled system and the heat transfer relationships, the amplitude of temperature fluctuations of the controlled system is gradually reduced to ensure ultra-high precision and excellent temperature stability for both the telescope and the detector. And then a test in the ground simulation system for the space environment was conducted to simulate the real thermal environment of the transit telescope, primary focal plane, and detector, and implemented multi-stage temperature control on the detector substrate. The final test results showed that the temperature fluctuation was controlled within ±3 mK, meeting the index requirement of ±10 mK, and it also exhibited a certain ability to resist environmental temperature fluctuations.

Items.Authors: Antoine Carré, Ralf Jedamzik, Ina Mitra, Florian Kanal, Janina Krieg
Items.Title: Resilience of a new optimized ZERODUR glass ceramic to ionizing radiations
Items.Abstract: A new Lithium-Alumino-Silicate glass ceramic further enhancing the properties of ZERODUR® in terms of thermo-mechanical hysteresis and long term stability is in development at SCHOTT. The form and thermal resilience of this material toward typical GEO ionizing radiations will be presented and the compatibility of this material with spaceborne applications will be discussed. This contribution will introduce the simulation made for characterizing the features of the ionizing particles over a GEO orbit. The ionizing particle type and their corresponding fluence for this orbit are then translated into imparted ionizing dose. These local imparted ionizing energy profiles are then reproduced at the laboratory using monoenergetic ionizing particle beams onto coupons. Possible deformations of these coupons induced by irradiation are quantified interferometrically, providing information about the expected level over the lifetime of a spaceborne optic.

Items.Authors: Nico Van der Merwe, Lisa Crause, Eben Wiid, Francois Strumpfer, Willem Van Der Westhuizen, Michael Sam, Nicolaas Jacobs, Denville Gibbons, Johan Hendricks
Items.Title: Restoring adjustment range in the SALT primary mirror: a systematic method for re-zeroing coarse and fine actuators
Items.Abstract: During the 2025 SALT shutdown, a major task was recovering global tip/tilt and piston adjustment of the segmented primary mirror. Several segments had reached the limits of their coarse actuators, with some close to the truss and others too far from it. A systematic procedure was developed to regain travel by making small, controlled adjustments to the coarse actuators while compensating with larger fine-actuator changes, keeping all segments within CCAS capture range. This allowed daytime mechanical work to be paired with nighttime CCAS-guided alignment without de-focusing the array. In total, 40 iterations were completed, restoring roughly 4 mm of usable travel to the most constrained segments.

Items.Authors: Ryan D. Hersey, Max Millar-Blanchaer, Skyler Palatnick, Jaren Ashcraft, Daniel Shanks, James K. Wallace, Tobias Wenger
Items.Title: Results from early prototyping of a metasurface polarization aberration corrector (PAC) for large observatories
Items.Abstract: Polarization aberrations pose a unique challenge for high contrast imaging as they cannot be corrected by traditional adaptive optics systems. They manifest as speckles in the imaging plane, masking as exoplanets. We present the simulated performance and in-lab characterization of a metasurface device for correcting the polarization aberrations generated by the mirrors of large telescopes.

Items.Authors: Robert W. Besuner, Jaime Cruz Duran
Items.Title: Retrofitting 6-meter primary mirrors to 4-meter telescopes for the Spec-S5 Experiment
Items.Abstract: A key performance improvement of the proposed Spec-S5 Stage 5 BAO experiment, relative to Stage 4 experiment DESI, is increased light-gathering enabled by installing 6-meter segmented primary mirrors on the existing Mayall and Blanco telescopes, replacing their monolithic 4-meter mirrors. This paper describes our engineering approach for upgrading the telescopes to accommodate the Spec-S5 optical and instrument elements, while maintaining full functionality of the existing telescope drives, maintaining telescope balance with no increase in supported mass, and facilitating integration of the new Spec-S5 optical and structural elements to the existing mounts.

Items.Authors: Jeffrey A. De Lucca, Alexandra N. Higley, Bridget C. O'Meara, Randall L. McEntaffer, Nathaniel Hamme, Ross C. McCurdy, James H. Tutt, Cooper B. Akers, Garrett A. Brady, Ivonne Ferrera, Aditi M. Gangadharan, Jake A. McCoy, Nolan McPhaul, Lily McEntaffer, Natasha Patel, Tristen M. Sextro, Joshua Wang, Vadim Burwitz, Gisela D. Hartner, Andreas Langmeier, Thomas G. Müller, Surangkhana Rukdee, Thomas Schmidt, David Colebrook, David Gopinath, Andrew D. Holland, Karen Holland, Daniel Evan, Stefano Basso, Alberto Moretti, Daniele Spiga, Casey T. DeRoo
Items.Title: Reverse telescope illumination of JET-X
Items.Abstract: To support the Pathfinder Off-Plane Grating Rocket Experiment (OGRE-P) suborbital rocket mission, the Joint European Telescope for X-ray Astronomy (JET-X) optic must be fully illuminated under laboratory conditions. We demonstrate a cost-effective alignment method using optical light and a hobbyist Dobsonian telescope operated in reverse to generate a large-diameter collimated beam. This approach minimizes expense while achieving the necessary illumination for calibration. We present technical details of the instrumentation setup and alignment procedure to enable other researchers to replicate this low-cost technique for similar large-aperture optical systems.

Items.Authors: Priscila Pires, Victor Echeverria, Francisco Gajardo
Items.Title: Review of the stripping process for aluminum coating in NOIRLab
Items.Abstract: This work, conducted by AURA/NOIRLab and La Serena University, investigates how to optimize the chemical stripping process used to remove aluminum coatings from the Blanco 4-m and SOAR telescope mirrors. Although high-quality coatings are essential for optical performance, current stripping methods have changed little over time and lack clarity regarding efficiency and reaction mechanisms. The study followed three stages: reproducing existing procedures, testing controlled variations in concentration and application methods, and evaluating acidic, basic, and redox solutions through visual inspection and conductivity measurements. Results show that a single well-formulated acidic or basic solution can fully remove aluminum, eliminating the traditional multi-step sequence. The next steps are to apply these results to telescope mirrors and quantify gains in time, chemical use, safety, and waste reduction.

Items.Authors: Nicolas Blind, Bruno Chazelas, Muskan Shinde, Isaac Dinis, Nathanaël Restori, Bachar Wehbe, Leonie Hoerner, Christophe Lovis, Mary Angelie M. Alagao, Romain Fétick, Vincent Chambouleyron, Cédric Taïssir Héritier Salama, Benoît Neichel, Jean-François Sauvage, Thierry Fusco, Sylvain Cetre
Items.Title: RISTRETTO front-end: entering the PDR phase
Items.Abstract: RISTRETTO is a diffraction-limited visible instrument using high-dispersion coronagraphy to detect and characterize nearby rocky exoplanets such as Proxima Centauri b. Its Front-End enables high-contrast single-mode fiber injection at 2 λ/D and includes an XAO system, a coronagraphic IFU based on the new PIAAN concept, and a high-precision closed-loop ADC. Recent milestones include the laboratory demonstration of PIAAN, on-sky validation of the NIR unmodulated pyramid WFS, and deployment of the DD4AO real-time controller. These results support consolidated XAO simulations, a complete error budget, and the tolerance analyses needed to launch detailed Front-End design. We present these developments and report the outcomes of the System Architecture Review ahead of the PDR phase.

Items.Authors: Nathanaël Restori, Nicolas Blind, Bruno Chazelas, Christophe Lovis, Christoph Mordasini, Muskan Shinde
Items.Title: RISTRETTO: two-photon polymerization (2PP) 3D printing and glass laser micro-fabrication for singlemode integral field units (IFUs)
Items.Abstract: RISTRETTO is a diffraction-limited instrument for detecting the reflected light from exoplanets in the visible. One of its core components is a seven-spaxels IFU made of single mode fibers. Due to their small core size, the alignment tolerances between fibers and micro-lens are extremely tight, on the order of a few hundreds of nanometers. This ensures efficiency and proper sky coverage. The coupling efficiency requirement for RISTRETTO is xx% [Blind et al. same conference]. This is the design driver. These tolerances are difficult to acheive using traditional techniques. We present the results of our prototyping activities, showing the performances obtained using Two-Photon Polymerization (2PP) 3D printing and glass laser micro-fabrication.

Items.Authors: Logan Pawlowski, Nicolas Hernandez, Amit Ashok
Items.Title: Robust and compact origami pyramid wavefront sensor design for small telescopes
Items.Abstract: In this work, we present the hardware and software methodologies underlying a compact, robust, and unmodulated pyramid wavefront sensor. We outline a practical design procedure tailored for single-conjugate adaptive optics on small- to medium-aperture telescopes, and describe our hardware integration with our machine learning wavefront reconstructor. This design introduces a folded-path “origami pyramid” architecture that substantially shortens track length, relaxes manufacturing and alignment tolerances, and potentially reduces fabrication cost. Furthermore, our transformer-based neural network provides improved wavefront estimation in nonlinear regimes, where traditional interaction-matrix reconstructors fail in the absence of modulation.
